manifest.title: Cap
manifest.tagline: Open source screen recording and sharing, a Loom alternative
manifest.description:
Cap is an open source alternative to Loom: record your screen and camera, then share a link
that plays instantly in the browser, with comments, reactions, transcriptions and AI summaries.

This is an **unofficial community package**, not affiliated with or supported by Cap Software.
It runs Cap's official `cap-web` and `cap-media-server` images, unmodified, in one container.

### What you need

* **S3-compatible object storage** for recordings (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, ...). Cloudron
  has no object-storage addon, so the bucket and its credentials are configured in
  `/app/data/env.sh`. Recordings are therefore **not** part of Cloudron backups.
* Optionally a **Resend** account, so Cap can email login links. Cap does not support other
  mail providers, so the Cloudron mail server can't be used.
* Free disk space of about three times your largest recording, for transcoding.

The database (MySQL) is provided by Cloudron and is included in backups.
manifest.changelog:
* Initial package: Cap web + media server from the official images, Cloudron MySQL, external S3 storage
* Media server bound to 127.0.0.1 and run in production mode
* Writable Next.js build dir (runtimeDirs) and workflow state in /app/data
* env.sh: syntax check before use, AssemblyAI/AI provider settings, concurrency knob
* env.sh may only contain plain NAME="value" lines (it is read as root)
* One video transcode at a time by default; warning when sign-up is open to anyone
* Daily cleanup of finished video-processing job state older than WORKFLOW_RETENTION_DAYS (30)
* Guard proxy in front of Cap: blocks custom S3 storage (SSRF to the Cloudron network), internal cron/workflow endpoints, and rate-limits OG images, the image optimizer, the Loom downloader and docs AI
manifest.postInstallMessage:
Cap needs object storage before it can record anything.

1. Open the **File Manager** of this app and edit `/app/data/env.sh`.
2. Fill in the `CAP_AWS_*` and `S3_*` settings for your S3-compatible bucket and, optionally,
   `RESEND_API_KEY` / `RESEND_FROM_DOMAIN` for login emails.
3. **Restart** the app.

**Before sharing the URL:** set `CAP_ALLOWED_SIGNUP_DOMAINS` in `env.sh`, otherwise anyone can
sign up and upload recordings. On a server shared with other apps, also give Cap a CPU limit
(app → Resources); video transcoding uses ffmpeg.

manifest.changelog:
* Guard proxy: also catch no-JS server-action forms that use $ACTION_REF_ / JSON ids (incl. escaped ids); refuse action forms it cannot parse
* secrets.env is validated like env.sh and owned by root; Windows (CRLF) line endings are rejected with a clear error
* Image optimizer rate limit raised to 2000/min per IP (offices behind one NAT)
* Process stop timeouts fit Cloudron's 10 s grace period; clearer startup errors (MySQL wait, env file rules)
* README: rehearsed migration procedure, backups, rollback

manifest.changelog:
* env file validator: only space and tab count as blanks (vertical tab / form feed allowed command execution as root), whitespace required before a trailing comment, control characters rejected
* Guard proxy: inspect form posts on every path (Next routing is case-sensitive, so /API/x is a page), match only $ACTION_ fields, deliver the 413 response before dropping oversized uploads
* Stop timeouts add up to less than Cloudron's 10 s grace period (supervisor stops programs sequentially)

manifest.changelog:
